motivation: The initialization diagnostic measured raw gradient changes. AdamW divides by its retained second moment, so those changes cannot be equated with proportional optimizer updates.
proof_targets: Positive or arbitrary scalar rescaling of every input and initial buffer rescales the existing exponential moment recurrence by the same scalar.

For one fixed c>0 applied to an entire supplied gradient history and epsilon>0, the bias-corrected Adam direction at epsilon equals the unscaled-history direction at epsilon/c. Retain both zero-initialized moment histories and the completed-update clock.

Starting from the same parameter and zero buffers, the native AdamW recurrence driven by c*g at epsilon has the same complete parameter trajectory as the recurrence driven by g at epsilon/c, with first moments multiplied by c and second moments by c^2. Use the same arbitrary rate schedule and decoupled decay. Gradients are supplied sequences, not gradients assumed unchanged after a model intervention.

profile_rules.constant: multiplier 1 at every zero-indexed update k
profile_rules.alternating: multiplier 1 when k is even, -0.5 when k is odd
profile_rules.delayed_pulse: multiplier 0 for k<16, 1 for 16<=k<32, -1 for 32<=k<48, 0 thereafter

arms.scaled: c times represented gradients, epsilon unchanged

numerical_grid.reference: Independent 80-digit Decimal recurrence evaluated on actual represented initial parameters, gradients and Python scalar hyperparameters; check every parameter, first moment and second moment vector at all64 updates in both arms.
numerical_grid.comparison_count_note: 64 updates times nine vector comparisons: both arms versus independent reference (six), plus direct parameter/first-moment/second-moment scaling identities (three).
numerical_grid.policy: Retain every vector and all failures. No changed tolerances after execution. Check the independent reference and compile the proofs, then commit all validated sources before the18 traces.

limits: Real-arithmetic identities concern a fixed positive factor across every supplied gradient in one coordinate and matching moment histories. A ratio of whole-layer gradient RMS values does not satisfy that condition.

Model initialization changes parameters and may change gradient directions, future gradients, tied-weight pathways and finite-epsilon RMS functions. These proofs do not identify two such training trajectories.
Optimizer epsilon is1e-8 and is distinct from the model RMS epsilon2^-23. Preserve both explicitly.
Synthetic CPU native AdamW checks do not validate fused or captured CUDA kernels, train a model, evaluate task data, choose an initializer or prove convergence.
